facts.claim: After-purchase mail-in rebates for 2026/27 (April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027). The application must reach the AEA within 3 months of the purchase date. A household can get up to two rebates on the same type of product per fiscal year (except thermostats, ECM pumps, LED lighting and plug-in controllers). Rebates are no longer available on LED lighting in hydro communities or on heating systems that use fossil fuels.
facts.amount: Wood stove 50% of purchase cost up to $2,000. Wood pellet stove 50% up to $2,000. Programmable thermostat 50% up to $150 (up to 5 a year for an individual). ECM pump 50% up to $500. Drain water heat recovery system (30% efficiency or better) $700. Automated vehicle plug-in controller 50% up to $150. Washing machine $200. Ventless dryer $500. All-in-one washer and ventless dryer $750.
facts.eligibility: NWT residents, businesses, non-profits and governments. ENERGY STAR certification needed for some products.
facts.notes: Read in the browser on 2026-10-21. Office: 101-5102 51st Street, Yellowknife, 867-920-3333.

facts.claim: Rebates for insulating the home, claimed with the Residential Insulation Rebate Application Form.
facts.amount: Exterior wall insulation up to $8,000. Ceiling insulation up to $1,500. Exposed floor insulation $500. Basement insulation up to $2,500. Basement header insulation $625. Crawlspace insulation up to $2,000.
facts.eligibility: NWT residents. The amount-per-area rules are in the AEA guidelines, which were not read.

facts.claim: Funding for solar, wind, wood pellet heating, biofuel and ground-source heat pumps. Distributed first come, first served, with pre-approval, subject to funds. The AEA can no longer offer rebates on grid-connected renewable electricity projects in communities that use hydroelectricity. The AEA asks you to contact them before applying.
facts.amount: Residents: up to $30,000 for biomass-fueled heating systems such as wood-pellet boilers; up to $20,000 for all other projects such as solar photovoltaic systems. The rebate is the lower of 50% of eligible costs or a savings calculation (for solar electric projects, $4.00 per watt).
facts.eligibility: NWT residents, businesses, non-profits and governments.

facts.program: Northwest Territories air-source heat pump rebate
facts.claim: We found no AEA rebate for air-source heat pumps on its Energy-Efficient Products or Renewable Energy pages on October 21, 2026. Ground-source heat pumps are listed under Renewable Energy. The AEA's news list includes a June 9, 2026 study of how well heat pumps work in Yellowknife.
facts.notes: A negative: we did not find one, which is not proof none exists.
